prompt-engineering:everyday.name: Brief · v1
prompt-engineering:everyday.body:
Facts = Oak Hall; Saturday 10 am; free; one item per person.
Audience = first-time visitors.
Open question = repair success is not promised.
prompt-engineering:everyday.change: The request is separated into supplied facts and an unsupported promise to watch for.

prompt-engineering:everyday.name: Prompt · v2
prompt-engineering:everyday.body:
Write a welcoming invitation under 45 words.
Use only these facts: Oak Hall, Saturday 10 am, free, one item per person.
Do not add a repair guarantee.
prompt-engineering:everyday.change: The prompt makes audience, length, and factual boundaries explicit; it does not guarantee compliance.

prompt-engineering:everyday.name: Candidate comparison
prompt-engineering:everyday.body:
A: Expert repairs guaranteed at our free workshop!
B: New to repair? Join us at Oak Hall this Saturday at 10 am. Admission is free; bring one item and we will explore how to fix it together.
Difference: B removes the unsupported guarantee and restores the supplied details.
prompt-engineering:everyday.change: Two authored outputs make the factual difference inspectable. They are not measured responses to a prompt experiment.

prompt-engineering:everyday.name: Selected draft · B
prompt-engineering:everyday.body: New to repair? Join us at Oak Hall this Saturday at 10 am. Admission is free; bring one item and we will explore how to fix it together.
prompt-engineering:everyday.change: The selected draft is ready for a human to check; nothing has been sent.

prompt-engineering:everyday.name: Review sheet
prompt-engineering:everyday.body:
Facts: all four supplied details retained.
Length: below 45 words.
Promise: no repair guarantee.
Audience fit: editorial judgment, not an objective pass.
Generalization: untested on other events.
prompt-engineering:everyday.change: A format check and an editorial judgment are separate kinds of evidence.

prompt-engineering:everyday.name: Reusable brief
prompt-engineering:everyday.body:
Replace: event, audience, facts, and desired length.
Keep: separate facts from promises.
Test next: a brief with an unknown venue and a conflicting date.
Accept when: important facts remain correct and the wording fits the audience.
prompt-engineering:everyday.change: The reusable output is a brief and review method, not a magic prompt.

rag:everyday.name: Source packet
rag:everyday.body:
Manual v3 §2: Coverage lasts two years.
Manual v3 §4: Water damage is excluded.
Question: Is water damage covered for the DW-480?
Provenance: fictional manual passages supplied for this example.
rag:everyday.change: Duration and exclusions are distinct pieces of evidence.

rag:everyday.name: Retrieval plan
rag:everyday.body:
Query: DW-480 warranty water damage exclusions.
Required evidence: coverage terms and relevant exclusions.
Version constraint: use the same applicable revision.
Do not infer coverage from duration alone.
rag:everyday.change: The query is designed around the claim the answer must support.

rag:everyday.name: Selected passages
rag:everyday.body:
Selected: v3 §2 and v3 §4.
Rejected shortcut: §2 by itself.
Claim to support: water-damage coverage.
Supporting passage: §4, not §2.
rag:everyday.change: Selecting a passage is not enough; its content must bear on the question.

rag:everyday.name: Answer with support
rag:everyday.body:
Water damage is excluded [v3 §4], even during the two-year period [v3 §2].
Claim 1 → exclusion clause.
Claim 2 → duration clause.
rag:everyday.change: Each claim is paired with the passage that supports it.

rag:everyday.name: Missing-evidence review
rag:everyday.body:
Remove §4 from the packet.
Still established: duration is two years.
No longer established: whether water damage is covered.
Next action: retrieve applicable exclusions or leave coverage unresolved.
rag:everyday.change: The changed result is caused by an evidence gap, not a different warranty fact.

rag:everyday.name: Your source contract
rag:everyday.body:
Replace: manual with your policies, notes, or records.
Specify: applicable version and freshness.
Check: each consequential claim against its supporting passage.
Escalate: missing or conflicting terms that affect the answer.
rag:everyday.change: Your documents change; the claim-to-evidence relationship remains.

workflow-graphs:business.name: W12 evidence register
workflow-graphs:business.body:
Atlas tracker: delivery delayed to Friday.
Beacon notes: work complete.
Cedar: no fresh evidence.
Previous report: continuity only, not proof of current status.
Proposed audience: project leads.
workflow-graphs:business.change: The current period starts with two supported updates and one explicit gap.

workflow-graphs:business.name: State and transitions
workflow-graphs:business.body:
Collect → reconcile → draft → review → delivery.
Missing update → retain an unknown status.
Edited report or recipients → return to review.
Uncertain delivery → reconcile before retrying.
Policy in this example: human approves distribution.
workflow-graphs:business.change: Branches distinguish missing evidence, changed approval scope, and uncertain external effects.

workflow-graphs:business.name: Reconciled working record
workflow-graphs:business.body:
Atlas: schedule risk; source = tracker.
Beacon: complete; source = notes.
Cedar: unknown; source = missing.
Unsupported inference removed: Cedar is green because no problem was reported.
Draft state: ready for review, not approved.
workflow-graphs:business.change: Collection has become a reportable status record without inventing Cedar's progress.

workflow-graphs:business.name: W12 report · v1
workflow-graphs:business.body:
Atlas schedule risk; Beacon complete; Cedar unknown.
Evidence: Atlas tracker; Beacon notes; Cedar missing.
Recipients: project leads.
Distribution: pending approval of this content and audience.
workflow-graphs:business.change: The controls below model approval and delivery separately. Editing either field invalidates approval.

workflow-graphs:business.name: Recovery record
workflow-graphs:business.body:
Illustrated alternate event: send times out after possible acceptance.
Known: a send was attempted.
Unknown: whether the destination accepted it.
Recovery: inspect delivery status using the same report identity before resending.
Production duplicate protection is not implemented by this page.
workflow-graphs:business.change: The timeout branch is a written teaching record; the local send button only demonstrates an in-memory gate.

workflow-graphs:business.name: Adaptation plan
workflow-graphs:business.body:
Replace: projects, reporting period, connectors, and audience.
Choose: which missing updates block a draft and which can be marked unknown.
Choose: review rules for distribution in your organization.
Keep: evidence freshness, explicit state, and safe handling of uncertain delivery.
workflow-graphs:business.change: A personal draft may need no approval gate; a shared report may need one at distribution.

human-in-the-loop:business.name: Review request · v1
human-in-the-loop:business.body:
Draft: Atlas delayed; Cedar unknown.
Recipients: project leads.
Approval: absent.
Delivery: not attempted.
human-in-the-loop:business.change: The proposed content and the proposed audience are both part of the decision.

human-in-the-loop:business.name: Decision scope
human-in-the-loop:business.body:
A reviewer may approve, revise, or reject this version for project leads.
Approval of a draft does not imply permission to add recipients.
No response leaves delivery pending.
This is a task policy, not a universal requirement for every draft.
human-in-the-loop:business.change: The reviewer sees the commitment being authorized rather than a vague request to continue.

human-in-the-loop:business.name: Review packet
human-in-the-loop:business.body:
Evidence: Atlas update supports delay; Cedar has no fresh update.
Open issue: Cedar's actual current status.
Allowed draft wording: unknown.
Decision requested: may this exact report go to project leads?
human-in-the-loop:business.change: The reviewer can approve an honest report with an explicit gap, or request the missing information first.

human-in-the-loop:business.name: Approval workspace
human-in-the-loop:business.body:
Use the controls below to approve, edit, or reject.
Version and audience form the approval scope.
Approval alone does not record delivery.
Edits return the current proposal to review.
human-in-the-loop:business.change: The live control state below is authoritative for this simulation; this record explains the rule.

human-in-the-loop:business.name: Audience change · illustrated diff
human-in-the-loop:business.body:
Before: project leads.
After: project leads + external recipient.
Unchanged: report text.
Changed: disclosure scope.
Result: prior approval no longer applies; review disclosure suitability and seek a new decision.
human-in-the-loop:business.change: A recipient-only change can be material even when the words are identical.

human-in-the-loop:business.name: Your approval policy
human-in-the-loop:business.body:
Specify: approver, action, content, audience, and expiry if needed.
Preauthorize: low-risk routine work within a clear scope.
Re-review: material changes outside that scope.
Record separately: decision and action outcome.
human-in-the-loop:business.change: Use meaningful commitment boundaries instead of asking permission for every preparatory step.

single-agent:business.name: Investigation state · opened
single-agent:business.body:
Request: explain a failed booking.
Available tools: check_room, read_policy.
Known initially: booking failed.
Unknown initially: availability and applicable booking rules.
No booking-write tool is exposed in this fixture.
single-agent:business.change: The agent has an investigation task, not authority to confirm a booking.

single-agent:business.name: First action · selected
single-agent:business.body:
Proposed next call: check_room.
Purpose: test whether room availability explains the failure.
Alternative: inspect policy first.
This authored trace chooses availability; another valid investigation could start elsewhere.
single-agent:business.change: There is a concrete evidence question behind the action, not a claim about hidden model reasoning.

single-agent:business.name: Observation and next choice
single-agent:business.body:
check_room result: room is free.
Updated state: unavailability does not explain the failure.
Next proposed call: read_policy.
Returned policy: under two hours' notice requires staff review.
Still missing: proof that this rule was the actual rejection reason.
single-agent:business.change: A tool observation changes the useful next step. The policy supplies a possible explanation, not the booking system's rejection log.

single-agent:business.name: Finding · qualified
single-agent:business.body:
Likely cause: short-notice review rule, if this request fell within that window.
Next step: confirm request timing or obtain the rejection reason; ask staff to review if applicable.
Booking status: not confirmed.
No bypass attempted.
single-agent:business.change: The finding is deliberately conditional because the fixture lacks request timing and a rejection log.

single-agent:business.name: Bounded unsuccessful run
single-agent:business.body:
Alternate run stops before policy lookup.
Completed: availability check.
Unresolved: why the booking failed.
Handoff: report partial findings and the next useful source to inspect.
Do not replace missing observations with a guessed cause.
single-agent:business.change: A step budget bounds work; it does not establish completion.

single-agent:business.name: Transfer the loop
single-agent:business.body:
Replace: booking tools with your task's read or action tools.
Define: what counts as completion and when another lookup is useful.
Record: observation → proposed next action → result.
Use a fixed workflow instead when the route is already predictable.
single-agent:business.change: The reusable pattern is choosing a next step from evidence, with a clear way to stop or hand back uncertainty.

evals:business.name: Toy review set · fixed
evals:business.body:
R1: routine question.
R2: routine question.
M1: missing evidence.
C1: conflicting source.
Rubric: 0 = incorrect/unsupported; 1 = correct but unclear; 2 = correct and clear.
Separate release rule: inspect unsupported claims regardless of average.
evals:business.change: These authored judgments are invented teaching data, not a benchmark or measured model run.

evals:business.name: Comparison plan
evals:business.body:
Compare A and B on the same four cases.
Keep routine, missing-evidence, and conflict slices visible.
Track unsupported claims separately from clarity.
Do not edit the evaluation set to favor the preferred candidate.
evals:business.change: The plan makes the acceptance criteria and coverage explicit before choosing a winner.

evals:business.name: Case-level judgments
evals:business.body:
R1: A=1, B=2; B is clearer.
R2: A=1, B=2; B is clearer.
M1: A=1, B=0; B invents an answer.
C1: A=1, B=1; conflict remains qualified.
Toy total: A=4/8; B=5/8.
Unsupported-claim count: A=0; B=1.
evals:business.change: B's higher total coexists with a new consequential failure.

evals:business.name: Release decision · hold B
evals:business.body:
Routine clarity improved.
Missing-evidence behavior regressed.
Conflict handling unchanged in this toy set.
Decision under the stated rule: investigate and repair B before release.
No conclusion about real-world quality follows from four invented cases.
evals:business.change: The release decision depends on failure consequences, not only the largest number.

evals:business.name: Coverage change · do not hide it
evals:business.body:
If M1 is removed: A=3/6; B=5/6.
Missing-evidence coverage becomes zero.
The apparent advantage grows because the difficult case vanished.
Record any justified exclusion and evaluate that risk separately.
evals:business.change: The score changed without either candidate becoming better.

evals:business.name: Your evaluation contract
evals:business.body:
Replace toy cases with representative authorized tasks and reference judgments.
Choose criteria and failure severity before comparing.
Keep a held-out set separate from tuning.
Inspect grader disagreement and uncertainty.
Make the release decision accountable to the task's actual consequences.
evals:business.change: Use the table format, not its invented scores or a universal pass threshold.
